Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second innings of West Indies and the post-Tea session. The South African players make their way out to the middle, followed by Kraigg Brathwaite and Kieron Powell. If you are wondering why Kieron Powell when he is not in the original squad? He has been brought in as a concussion substitute for Nkrumah Bonner who was hit on the helmet in the first innings. Kagiso Rabada will start with the ball.
... Day 2, Session 3 ...

West Indies' bowlers toiled hard with the ball in hand. They gave it their all but it just was not their outing. Jason Holder was the star with a 4-fer but it was Jayden Seales who actually stole the show on Day 1 with 3 wickets but he was unlucky on Day 2. Roach was decent as well while the spinners had no help from the surface and they tried hard but to no reward. Right then, West Indies need to bat really, really well if they want to salvage something of the Test match. South Africa would look to pick up quick wickets and try to take some before Stumps on Day 2. Join us in around 20 minutes for the final session of Day 2.

South Africa did not start off well as they lost Dean Elgar in the first over and then Keegan Petersen soon after. Aiden Markram played a fine knock of 60 before he fell towards the end of Day 1. Rassie van der Dussen looked good but it was the knock of Quinton de Kock that made the difference. He came out, started slowly, and then after losing partners at the other end, he went berserk. De Kock scored 141 runs and many of them came in the partnership between him and Anrich Nortje. He is one of the reasons that South Africa lead by so much.

Quinton de Kock, take a bow! What an unbelievable innings from de Kock! His 141 has helped the Proteas score 322 and they lead by 225 runs. They are well ahead in the game and they will look to start well with the ball. West Indies have a big task in hand as they are way behind and they need to bat very well to have a chance in this game. With the last wicket, it is TEA as well.

Welcome back for the second session of Day 2! The West Indies' players stride out to the middle, followed by Quinton de Kock and Wiaan Mulder. Jason Holder will start with the ball.
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

West Indies started the day poorly as they bowled some loose deliveries and allowed the South African batters to settle. Once Holder was introduced, he put a stop to the free flow of runs and bowled on some tight line and length. His efforts paid off as he dismissed Rassie van der Dussen with a peach of a delivery. Seales and Roach too were decent and troubled Mulder to some extent but no reward. They will be looking to bundle the South African batters out soon and avoid a huge lead onto them. Join us at 12.40 pm local (1640 GMT) for the second session of Day 2.

Another good session for South Africa! They are right on top in this game! South Africa started their day well with de Kock scoring two boundaries in the first over itself. Van der Dussen too looked good and supported de Kock well at the other end. After Holder was introduced into the attack, the South African batters found it tough to score runs off his bowling. Rassie van der Dussen fell but Quinton de Kock is looking in fine touch. Wiaan Mulder struggled at the start but has settled himself in and is looking really good. The visitors would now look to continue churning out the runs and push West Indies out of the game.

We are all set to begin Day 2! The West Indies' players stride out to the middle, followed by Rassie van der Dussen and Quinton de Kock. Kemar Roach will start with the ball for the hosts.

Jayden Seales is there for a chat. He says it is an amazing feeling on debut. He adds that they will try to do the basic things like yesterday and try to bowl South Africa out early. He mentions that he has received great encouragement from Sir Curtly Ambrose and it is a special feeling to receive a cap from him.

Pitch report - Mike Haysman is there for the pitch report. He says that it was a tough Day 1 for the batsmen. Adds that there were plenty of play and misses. Stacy-Ann King says that this pitch has been really interesting for the bowlers and there are nice indentations and it is going to offer a lot for the seamers. Tells that there is moisture and the seamers are going to have a good time in the first session.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 2 of the first Test between West Indies and South Africa. South Africa had a top Day 1 as they bowled out West Indies for 97 in their first innings and despite losing some quick wickets towards the end while batting, they are well on top and would look to score as much as possible. West Indies, on the other hand, are not out of it yet as Jayden Seales starred on debut with the ball and now they would look to wrap up the South African innings as quickly as possible. What will happen? Stay tuned to find out.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

Right then! That is all we have for you from Day 1. This Test is nicely poised with South Africa being just in front with a lead of 31. Do join us for Day 2 on 11th June 2021, it starts at 1000 local (1400 GMT) but our build-up starts before that. Till then, stay safe and goodbye!

Lungi Ngidi is down for a chat, says that it is not very often that you bowl a team out for 97. Adds that they looked to execute their plans and wanted to be ruthless with their line and lengths after losing the toss. Further adds that it's been a while since he was able to put in a performance like this and he has been working hard behind the scenes. Says the slip cordon works really hard. Tells that it was amazing to take 5 wickets as it has been a while for him since he took one.

Earlier in the day, West Indies were bowled out for 97, which is their lowest score against South Africa in Tests. First, it was Anrich Nortje who rocked their top order with his four wickets and then Lungi Ngidi wrapped things up with his 5-wicket haul. Kagiso Rabada also took a wicket after bowling well in his first spell. For West Indies, none of their batters clicked with Jason Holder being the highest-scorer with 20 runs.

Kemar Roach gave a dream start to West Indies when he picked Dean Elgar in the first over, but after that, it was all about the debutant, Jayden Seales. He took the wicket of Keegan Petersen in his first over and when the Aiden Markram - Rassie van der Dussen stand was getting threatening, he dismissed Markram with a peach of a delivery. Seales went on to dismiss Kyle Verreynne soon after to rock the South African batting. Now, on Day 2, they will look to restrict South Africa to a low score.

The South African innings started in the worst possible manner with Dean Elgar getting out in the first over. Keegan Petersen played a few strokes but got out soon. But then came a good partnership between Aiden Markram and Rassie van der Dussen. They batted with patience and saw their team to safety. Aiden Markram would have wanted to bat till Stumps but he was out towards the fag end of the day and the debutant Kyle Verreynne could not make much of a difference. On Day 2, the priority for them will be to extend the lead as much as possible.

A day of Test cricket that belonged to the bowlers, with 14 wickets falling on the day. South Africa have a lead of 31 runs but West Indies are still in the game. The highest score on Day 1 was 60, it is something that you don't often see in modern-day cricket.

Right then! The mantra for both the teams in the final session is simple, South Africa would look to get a solid partnership and West Indies will look to take wickets. But what will the scoreboard say at the end of Day 1? We will find out. The final session coming up at 1500 local( 1900 GMT).

Earlier in the session, South Africa didn't take much time wrapping the West Indies batting. Lungi Ngidi was the man of the hour scalping a fifer. Holder played some good attacking shots towards the end before getting out. He managed to raise his team's score to 97 as other batters failed to deal with the South African pace attack.

The South African batting didn't have the best start as Dean Elgar departed in the first over itself. Though Elgar departed early, Aiden Markram and the debutant, Keegan Petersen have looked good. Markram would consider himself lucky as he got almost carried through to the keeper off Kemar Roach. Other than that, he looks settled at the crease and Petersen too looks good. They will look to stitch a partnership in the last session and mount a huge lead on the Windies.

West Indies started their bowling well as Roach dismissed the South African skipper with a peach of a delivery. West Indies needed an early breakthrough and they got one. After that, they have been bowling consistently well into the right lengths. However, they would still hope to get a few nicks early in the next session as they don't have a respectable total on the board. Their aim would be to not allow the South African batters to settle and get crucial breakthroughs.

Another session that has belonged to South Africa. They did lose Dean Elgar in the first over of their innings but still, they are well on top of this game. West Indies need to take quick wickets to get back in the hunt.

EDGY FOUR! Markram would have had his heart in his mouth there. Roach pitches it on length, nipping away. The ball finds the outside edge of Aiden Markram and went between the diving keeper and first-slip towards the third man fence. A lucky boundary for Markram.
Length delivery, on off. Markram chooses not to play.

Pitches it down the leg side, Markram lets it sail through.
FOUR! Kept it fuller on leg, Markram flicks it towards fine leg for a boundary. The keeper dives to his left but the ball was just outside his reach.
Good length delivery, on off. Petersen taps it to third man for a couple.

Short delivery on leg, Peterson has a touch on it. The ball fell just short of keeper. The ball rolls to the fine leg. Petersen takes a couple.

Jason Holder to share the new ball from the other end.

Keegan Petersen walks out to bat on his Test debut.

OUT! CAUGHT! Kemar Roach removes the skipper early. Good length delivery, on off, angling away from the batsman. Elgar has a poke at it but finds the outside edge. The ball flies to Jermaine Blackwood at the second slip. He takes a good catch diving to his left and Dean Elgar has to depart early. This is what the Windies would have wanted. They have struck early.
